title: Uninsured Hit and Run Accidents in New York, NY: What You Need to Know
metaDescription: Learn about uninsured hit and run accidents in New York, NY, including statistics, laws, and what steps to take after an incident.
excerpt: Educational New York, NY guide — 3-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Confirm coverage at the scene
paragraphs: Ask for insurance card photos and verify policy status. In New York, uninsured motorist rates track with statewide averages — always assume minimum limits until verified.

sections.heading: Your UM/UIM policy in New York
paragraphs: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage on your policy may pay when the at-fault driver has no coverage or insufficient 25/50/10 limits.
Notify your carrier promptly; UM claims still require documentation of injuries and damages.

sections.heading: Hit-and-run steps in New York
paragraphs: Report hit-and-runs immediately to New York police. UM coverage often requires a police report within 24–72 hours.
Seek witnesses and camera footage near Cross Bronx Expressway.

sections.heading: Medical and financial documentation
paragraphs: Use NYU Langone if injured. Track lost wages and transportation costs.

sections.heading: When litigation may be necessary
paragraphs: If UM/UIM carriers deny or lowball offers, a licensed New York attorney can evaluate bad-faith and negligence claims against the at-fault driver directly.

sections.heading: New York medical resources after a crash
paragraphs: New York residents often use NYU Langone, NewYork-Presbyterian, Bellevue Hospital after serious collisions. Level I trauma care is available at Bellevue Hospital.
Document every provider visit — gaps in treatment are a common reason NY insurers reduce settlement offers.
Keep receipts for prescriptions, imaging (MRI/CT), physical therapy, and medical transport.
list: Photograph visible injuries the same day when safe
Follow discharge instructions and keep all after-visit summaries
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for the adjuster

sections.heading: Local crash patterns: FDR Drive, West Side Highway, Brooklyn-Queens Expressway, I-95
paragraphs: The metro area sees roughly 45,000 reported crashes annually (est.). High-risk areas include Cross Bronx Expressway; Brooklyn-Queens Expressway; FDR Drive.
If your collision occurred near FDR Drive, note mile markers, exit numbers, and direction of travel for the police report.
New York DOT data is available via https://www.dot.ny.gov/ — useful when disputing fault or road conditions.

sections.heading: New York County (Manhattan) reports, courts, and evidence
paragraphs: Request the official crash report through local law enforcement. New York County Supreme Court handles many civil injury filings in the region.
Business security video near New York retail corridors is often deleted within 7–30 days — send preservation letters quickly when appropriate.
The New York City Bar Association offers lawyer-referral resources; WreckMatch LLC can also connect you with independent New York attorneys at no obligation.

sections.heading: Educational disclaimer
paragraphs: WreckMatch LLC is a legal referral service — not a law firm. This New York guide is general education only and does not create an attorney-client relationship.
Laws and insurance rules change; verify all deadlines, coverage, and rights with a licensed New York attorney before making decisions about your claim.

sections.heading: Settlement timeline expectations in New York
paragraphs: Minor property-damage claims in New York may resolve in weeks, but injury claims involving treatment, lost wages, or disputed fault often take months. Insurers may request recorded statements, independent medical exams, and broad medical authorizations — review each request carefully.
New York uses Pure comparative comparative negligence with a 3-year statute of limitations for most injury cases. Calendar your deadline from the date of injury.
If you were transported from FDR Drive to NYU Langone, keep ambulance, ER, and follow-up bills organized. UM/UIM and MedPay endorsements may apply when the other driver is underinsured.
list: Do not accept the first settlement check if treatment is ongoing
Avoid discussing fault on social media
Request adjuster denials or reservations of rights in writing
Compare repair estimates with your insurer's appraisal
Consult a licensed attorney before signing general releases

sections.heading: Document checklist for New York claims
paragraphs: Organize a folder (physical or digital) for every document tied to your New York crash: police report number, insurance claim numbers, tow and storage receipts, and rental car agreements.
Request itemized medical bills from NYU Langone rather than summary statements — itemized bills help catch billing errors and support future negotiations.
list: Photos of all vehicles and the scene from multiple angles
Employer note for any missed work shifts
Insurance adjuster name, phone, and claim number
Repair estimates from at least two body shops

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in New York?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 3-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.

faq.question: Will my rates increase if I use UM/UIM coverage?
faq.answer: Rules vary by carrier and state. Ask your insurer in writing; using UM after a not-at-fault crash is often protected — verify your policy.

faq.question: Where can I get a crash report in New York?
faq.answer: Contact the investigating agency listed on your exchange-of-information form. New York County (Manhattan) reports may also be available through local police or https://www.dot.ny.gov/.
